question: The Jhaveri sisters- Nayana, Suverna, Ranjana and Darshana are famously associated with which style of dance?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Manipuri.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• **Nayana, Ranjana, Suvarna, **and **Darshana Jhaveri **began dancing together on stage in the **1950s **both in India and overseas.
 
• In 1956, they were the first non-Manipuris to perform their dances at the **Govindji Temple **inside the royal palace of **Imphal**.
 
• The sisters eventually founded the **Manipuri Nartanalaya **in **1972 **alongside their **Guru **and **Kalavati Devi **in **Mumbai, Kolkata, and Imphal.**
 
• Over time, their name came to be **associated **with **Manipuri dance.**
 
• Before taking up the role herself, **Darshana **assisted her guru in **teaching, research, **and **choreography **over the years and has written a number of books and papers on the dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Kathakali: **

 
 
• It is a significant type of **classical Indian dance**.
 
• The extremely **colourful **make-up and costumes worn by the **traditional **male **actor**-**dancers **set this "**story play**" kind of art apart.
 
• It is indigenous to **Kerala's Malayalam**-speaking southwest region, where Malayalis predominately **practise **and enjoy it.**​**
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam:**
 
 
• **​**It is a significant type of **classical Indian dance**** **that has its roots in **Tamil **Nadu. 
 
• It reflects South Indian **religious themes **and **spiritual ideals**, primarily those of **Shaivism **and generally of Hinduism.
 
• It is one of the **eight internationally **renowned Indian classical dance genres.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi:**
 
 
• **​**One of the eight principal classical dances of India is called **Kuchipudi**.
 
• It comes from the **Andhra Pradesh **state of India, specifically the village of Kuchipudi.
 
 

ec:T
